name: DSH Remote — Mobile Chat Design Tokens
description: The semantic token layer for the DSH Remote mobile client. Code depends on token NAMES only; the values below are the design-time defaults and may be re-themed without touching component contracts. No credential, machine path, API secret or runtime token may ever be added to this file.

breakpoints.comment: 360-479 single-column mobile; 480-767 large mobile; >=768 tablet with a persistent session rail. 390x844 is the primary design viewport.

spacing.comment: The complete spacing scale. No component may use a value outside this scale.

rules.comment: 14px is the floor for any body text. Primary chat body is 15px, which is inside the required 15-16px band.

surface.comment: Neutral charcoal surfaces sampled from the DSH Desktop chat and composer reference. The composer sits on the raised #2C2C2E surface over the #141416 chat canvas.

border.comment: R8G: `subtle` exists so a region boundary can be stated without the full weight of `default`. Three weights let message, composer and rail separate by degrees rather than by one hard line.

color.comment: Dark-first palette for a restrained technical client. Every status colour has a paired icon/text cue; colour alone never conveys state (see accessibility).

touchTarget.comment: Any primary interactive element is at least 44x44 CSS px, including the code-block copy button.

message.comment: User and assistant bubbles cap at 85% of the content width. Assistant code blocks may use the full available content width and scroll horizontally rather than widen the page. R8G: groupGapPx was 12 and bubblePaddingPx was 12 — both raised so consecutive messages read as distinct groups and bubbles are not cramped at 360px.

elevation.comment: R8G: a restrained two-step shadow scale. Depth is stated once per region — a raised composer seat and a floating overlay — rather than decorating every surface. No blur-heavy or coloured shadows.

layout.comment: The composer grows with content up to 40% of the viewport height, then scrolls internally so the timeline keeps usable space.

reducedMotion.comment: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce removes transform and looping motion; state remains conveyed by icon and text.

accessibility.comment: Focus is always visible and never removed. Status is never conveyed by colour alone.

zIndex.comment: Ordered layers; no component may invent a higher value.
